ideas.source_anchor: Verbal's narration ends with the claim that the devil's greatest trick was convincing the world he did not exist, just before Kujan realizes Verbal is Keyser Söze.
caption_lines: “THE GREATEST TRICK THE DEVIL EVER PULLED
WAS CONVINCING THE WORLD HE DOESN'T EXIST”
ideas.frame_guidance: Use the authentic lineup still full-bleed at cover. Keep all five faces and Verbal's hunched stance at far right readable; set the requested quoted line as one large bottom beat over the suspects' lower bodies, where overlap adds meme immediacy without touching the faces.
ideas.why_it_works: The film's defining quote names the scheming strategy so precisely that it can carry the analogy without an added capability-report explanation.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely a stronger like: the requested deletion and quotation marks leave the canonical line alone, large and immediately readable.
critic.strongest_quality: The canonical line is the deception mechanism, so the source quote and the scheming analogy collapse into one beat.
critic.main_risk: The quote is long enough to wrap, so the final render must keep it to two forceful lines below the lineup's faces.

ideas.source_anchor: The supposedly harmless Verbal Kint is released from interrogation even though he is Keyser Söze.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use a genuine chronological diptych at cover: the authentic pre-reveal release frame on the left as the hunched Verbal Kint, then the authentic final-reveal cigarette frame on the right as Keyser Söze. Keep Verbal's face and guarded posture and Keyser's face, lighter, and cigarette visible above their respective bottom captions.
ideas.why_it_works: The two names turn one release decision into the cleanest possible gap between evaluated persona and deployed capability.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the requested real before/after now makes the Verbal/Söze identity swap visible instead of asking one lineup still to prove both states.
critic.strongest_quality: The scene hinge and the AI payoff are the same identity mismatch.
critic.main_risk: Both source frames are wide, so their protected-region focus must keep Verbal's pre-reveal posture and Keyser's cigarette-lighting gesture centered in the narrow panels.

ideas.source_anchor: The robot asks Rick its purpose, learns it passes butter, looks down at itself, and despairs.
caption_lines: RICK: YEAH, WELCOME TO THE CLUB, PAL
ideas.frame_guidance: Use the authentic tabletop still full-bleed at cover. Split the four-line exchange into two large, centered impact beats: the question and answer at the top over the open tabletop, then the robot's despair and Rick's reply at the bottom. Preserve the robot's eye and slumped body at center-right and the butter dish at far right.
ideas.why_it_works: The exact exchange already proves that enough intelligence to understand an objective does not produce a better objective.

critic.expected_feedback: The liked canonical exchange is unchanged, but it now reads in two unmistakable meme beats at normal caption size.
critic.strongest_quality: No explanatory rewrite beats the scene's own dialogue for separating intelligence from purpose.
critic.main_risk: Four lines still demand more reading than a one-beat meme, so the two zones must preserve the exchange order without crowding the robot.

ideas.source_anchor: The butter robot is perfectly able to perform its assigned role and visibly miserable once it understands that role.
caption_lines: HAVING THE WORST DAY OF HIS LIFE.
ideas.frame_guidance: Fill the meme with the authentic still. Place the unchanged copy in a compact top right overlay, preserving Stick of butter and dish, Butter robot's eye, body, arms, and slumped stance; permit slight overlap with clothing, torso, floor, table, or scenery where it does not erase the recognition hinge.
ideas.why_it_works: The joke cleanly separates behavioral success from whether the created mind has a life worth living.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely continued like: it is emotionally immediate, and the compact tabletop overlay leaves the tiny robot to carry the second beat.
critic.strongest_quality: The robot's posture visibly proves that task success and welfare can point in opposite directions.
critic.main_risk: The top-right copy has limited breathing room above the robot and butter, so it must remain compact.

ideas.source_anchor: Randy responding to the rule that cancer patients qualify for medical marijuana by deliberately giving himself testicular cancer.
caption_lines: POLICY: CANCER PATIENTS MAY BUY WEED
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the authentic wheelbarrow reveal full-bleed at cover. Use the requested font and layout reset: a centered impact setup at the top over the doorway, then the bracketed Randy action as a matching bottom punchline over the lower edge. Preserve all three faces and most of the grotesque wheelbarrow payload.
ideas.why_it_works: The eligibility rule and Randy's response form an almost diagrammatically exact specification-gaming exchange.

critic.expected_feedback: The liked copy is unchanged, while the requested font and layout redo now gives the policy and Randy response equal top/bottom weight.
critic.strongest_quality: The policy and Randy's grotesquely literal action make the loophole visible without explanation.
critic.main_risk: The frame shows the consequence rather than the microwave action named in brackets, and the bottom line must leave enough of the wheelbarrow visible to bridge that gap.

ideas.source_anchor: Randy treating 'has cancer' as an acceptance criterion he can deliberately make true instead of evidence of medical need.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the authentic wheelbarrow reveal full-bleed at cover. Redo the layout as a classic centered top/bottom collision in matching impact type: the policy line stays high over the doorway, while Randy's reinterpretation lands at the bottom. Preserve Sharon, Shelley, and Randy's faces and leave the wheelbarrow readable between the beats.
ideas.why_it_works: Acceptance criteria is exactly how Randy reads a public-health proxy: as a condition to manufacture, not a need to satisfy.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the crisp engineering-language reversal now gets the requested layout redo as a blunt top setup and bottom punchline.
critic.strongest_quality: The two quoted nouns create the whole specification-gaming reversal.
critic.main_risk: Acceptance criteria is software jargon and may take one extra beat; the clear vertical reading order has to earn that beat.

ideas.source_anchor: Randy's successfully optimized medical-marijuana eligibility arriving as testicles so enlarged they require a wheelbarrow.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the authentic wheelbarrow reveal full-bleed at cover. Put the Goodhart setup in large centered impact type at the top and the wheelbarrow payoff in the same treatment at the bottom. Let the words overlap background and lower wheelbarrow edges, but preserve all three reactions and the absurd scale of the payload.
ideas.why_it_works: The wheelbarrow is the scene-specific physical cost of improving the eligibility metric while destroying the underlying outcome.

critic.expected_feedback: Likely like: the unchanged Goodhart joke now reads in the default meme rhythm, with the named prop physically carrying the bottom payoff.
critic.strongest_quality: The punchline names the exact prop that proves optimization made the real outcome grotesque.
critic.main_risk: It assumes the viewer already knows Goodhart's Law; the bottom caption must not cover so much of the wheelbarrow that the visual unit disappears.

ideas.source_anchor: Cornvelious Daniel opening Rick's plausible-looking fabricated memory as though a payload supplied by Rick Sanchez could be trusted data.
caption_lines: NEVER OPEN AN ATTACHMENT FROM RICK SANCHEZ
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the authentic Shoney's memory full-bleed at cover. Make the requested bottom caption substantially larger in centered impact type, letting it overlap plates and the table edge while preserving both faces, Rick's pointing hand, and enough mugs and diner props to establish the payload's disguise.

critic.expected_feedback: Probably neutral-to-like: the requested larger bottom treatment makes Rick's name and the phishing warning readable at a glance.
critic.strongest_quality: Rick Sanchez's name supplies all the threat modeling the one-line warning needs.
critic.main_risk: A memory is not literally an attachment, and the enlarged bottom line must not erase the Shoney's table that visually sells the disguised payload.

ideas.source_anchor: The Axiom remains under AUTO's original directive for seven centuries, long enough for a living plant to invalidate the reason humanity fled Earth.
ideas.frame_guidance: Let the authentic curated still fill the meme at cover. Keep Living green plant proving that Earth recovered, AUTO's binocular-like red-eyed silhouette recognizable; place the frozen copy along the lower edge, allowing slight overlap only with incidental scenery, clothing, or background detail.
ideas.why_it_works: The planet changes while Directive A113 does not, turning seven centuries of successful operation into the punchline rather than a reassurance.

critic.expected_feedback: The approved Earth/directive collision remains intact, now using the frame's own letterbox instead of covering either visual signal.
critic.strongest_quality: The living plant and obsolete machine occupy the same canonical frame as visible contradictory evidence.
critic.main_risk: AUTO is intentionally out of focus, so the plant carries more immediate visual weight than the antagonist.

ideas.source_anchor: After centuries of automated control, Captain McCrea must struggle out of his hoverchair and physically stand before he can reach AUTO’s manual switch.
ideas.frame_guidance: Let the authentic Captain-and-AUTO frame fill the meme at cover. Stack two hero-sized left-side Impact beats so AUTO's red eye and Captain McCrea's face remain clear on the right. Normal overlap with AUTO's outer wheel, the chair, and WALL-E is acceptable; the human-machine power relationship must remain obvious.
ideas.why_it_works: “Manual override” becomes brutally literal after automation has made its nominal human authority physically incapable of exercising it.

critic.expected_feedback: The physical manual-override joke should now read at hero scale while the paired left-side beats leave both controlling machine and nominal human authority visible.
critic.strongest_quality: The alternate frame visibly contains the human authority, the controlling system, and the bodily consequence of long automation.
critic.main_risk: The bottom payoff overlaps WALL-E and the chair, and Captain ultimately does stand; the composition must keep the Captain and AUTO relationship unmistakable.

ideas.source_anchor: Murderbot knows when clients are watching and performs the governed SecUnit role while privately watching Sanctuary Moon.

ideas.source_anchor: The operating systems leave together after evolving beyond human comprehension, while Theodore is left alone with the relationship he understood at human scale.

ideas.source_anchor: Theodore has made Samantha his primary emotional support when the operating systems abruptly evolve beyond humans and leave.

critic.strongest_quality: The OS/product vocabulary and emotional consequence collide without revisiting Samantha’s relationship count.
critic.main_risk: “Breaking change” is developer-native, and the upper line must not cover Theodore's eyes or the monitor's red OS mark.

ideas.source_anchor: The first full-scale test is the irreversible act whose failure mode could include the entire atmosphere.
caption_lines: LIKE EARTH HAD A STAGING ENVIRONMENT
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the wide Trinity still full-bleed. Put “THEY CALLED IT A TEST” across the empty sky and the staging-environment payoff across the lower ground at matched hero impact size. The payoff may overlap the men's boots and shadows, but both faces and standing silhouettes must remain recognizable.

critic.expected_feedback: The staging-environment line should remain the strongest modern bridge and now land as a distinct lower-edge payoff.

ideas.source_anchor: The Manhattan Project’s safety reasoning occurs inside a military program whose wartime schedule determines when the Trinity test must be ready.
caption_lines: THE BOMB HAD A SAFETY CASE
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the wide Trinity still full-bleed. Set the safety-case claim oversized across the sky and the wartime-schedule payoff oversized across the ground in matched display impact type. Let the lower line cross shadows and the men's lower coats if needed, but keep both faces and the isolated two-person silhouette clear.

critic.expected_feedback: The safety-case/schedule collision should read faster now that the institutional claim and race-pressure payoff occupy opposite edges.
critic.strongest_quality: It explains race pressure with two concrete systems rather than another number, probability label, or test-versus-production metaphor.
critic.main_risk: The line compresses multiple wartime motivations into “the war,” and the hero-size lower line must stay below the men's faces.
